---
title: Vivacious Cloud
description: How to launch Axolotl model training across multi-cloud GPU instances with Vivacious Cloud
---

[Vivacious Cloud](https://vivaciouscloud.com) is a multi-cloud GPU orchestration platform designed to provision compute and manage training workloads across heterogeneous providers (including AWS, RunPod, Lambda Labs, and GCP). 

Developers can manage and deploy training jobs using the official open-source companion CLI [`vivacious-cli`](https://github.com/Viavcious-cloud/vivacious-cli).

## Vivacious CLI Setup

Install the CLI globally via npm or clone from GitHub:

```bash
npm install -g vivacious-cli
```

Authenticate with your Vivacious Cloud account token:

```bash
vivacious login --token <YOUR_VIVACIOUS_TOKEN>
```

## Preparing and Deploying Workloads

### 1. Validate Dataset Structure

Before deploying compute, validate your training dataset format:

```bash
vivacious prepare --data ./dataset.jsonl
```

### 2. Request Hardware Permit

Vivacious Cloud manages server-authoritative GPU sizing and workload scheduling. Request a permit for your target GPU architecture:

```bash
vivacious permit --gpu-type A100 --hours 4
```

### 3. Deploy Training Job

Launch the provisioned workload using your issued permit:

```bash
vivacious deploy --name axolotl-llama3-job --permit-id <PERMIT_ID>
```

## Running Axolotl Training

On your provisioned GPU instance, clone Axolotl and install dependencies:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl.git
cd axolotl
pip install -e .
```

Launch fine-tuning using an existing configuration from the checkout:

```bash
accelerate launch -m axolotl.cli.train examples/llama-3/lora-8b.yml
```

Alternatively, fetch community examples using the Axolotl CLI:

```bash
axolotl fetch examples
```
